crime_highlights: Van Every came down to the basement where J.G. was watching TV, and asked him where the gun was
He told J.G. to wait downstairs, and walked upstairs with the gun
J.G. heard L.B. say something to Van Every, and then he heard a gunshot
J.G. saw L.B. on the ground, wounded, with Van Every standing in L.B.’s bedroom holding the gun
Van Every then stood over L.B. and threatened to put another bullet in him if he did not tell him where the money was
rationale_highlights: The trial judge accepted that it was likely that many of the appellant’s problems arose from intergenerational harm from his grandmother’s attendance at residential school
the trial judge recognized the Aboriginal status and history of the appellant, and expressly stated that he took them into consideration
The circumstances of the offence and the offender, without considering the Gladue factors, might well have justified a longer period of parole ineligibility.
note: Appeal court upholds judge's Gladue consideration; effect on sentence not quantified.

crime_highlights: the respondent attacked a jail guard, causing three puncture wounds to his neck
he stabbed his uncle in the neck
rationale_highlights: The sentencing judge was satisfied that the sentence he imposed properly reflected the Gladue principles that he was required to consider.
He was released with virtually no supports in place.
note: Gladue discussion is minimal; decision turns on dangerous offender law.

crime_highlights: J.N.D. was convicted of historic sexual offences against his cousin when she was a young girl
rationale_highlights: The trial judge then reviewed the Gladue principles extensively in her reasons and applied them to J.N.D.
the trial judge was making every effort to apply the principles mandated in Gladue
note: No offence narrative in decision; court does not state effect on culpability.
